column4: F: A common BricsCAD drawing. Can it become a costed order?
column5: F: Here is a common BricsCAD drawing set. Can it become a costed order? | M: Let's see. Two plans and an elevation, no markings, straight into the Modeller.

column4: M: Three raw sheets. No markings at all.
column5: M: A floor plan, a foundation plan and a South elevation. Raw: nothing marked, and no layer chosen for us. | F: So what does the Modeller know? | M: Only what the drawings say.

column3: W-DXF-SHED H1 + lane §L7.2 (suggestions yellow, never silent)
column4: M: It suggests only what the drawing states. In yellow.
column5: M: It suggests only what the drawing states. The units from the file header, the view and the name from the title. | F: Why yellow? | M: Yellow means suggested, not yet yours.

column3: W-DXF-SHED H2 (14 grid marks from dimension ticks, @Z=0 at the ground line y -4470.581) + F1 (foundation plan: 14 + 4)
column4: M: Accept all. The grid comes from the dimension ticks.
column5: M: Accept all. The grid comes from the dimension ticks, not from where the label text happens to sit. | F: And the height datum? | M: The ground line is zero.

column3: W-DXF-SHED H3 (SET, LEVEL, PL +24 in = 0.6096 m typed) · lane §L7.11
column4: M: Three facts only a person can state.
column5: M: Three facts only a person can state. The name of the set, the plan level, and the plinth datum: two feet above ground, read from the column detail. | F: Typed once? | M: Typed once.

column3: W-DXF-SHED H4 + W-DXF-STRUCT S1-S2 (body kinds in the Layers select)
column4: M: One decision: which layers are columns.
column5: M: One real decision. Layer Col is a column on the plans, layer zero is a column on the elevation. | F: And the rest? | M: Left alone.

column3: W-DXF-SHED F2 (32 columns built, 32 footings waiting under Body heights) · lane §L7.14
column4: M: The footings wait. No elevation shows them.
column5: M: No elevation shows the footings below ground, so the panel lists thirty-two as waiting. | F: Guessed depth? | M: Never. The depth is stated once, from the footing detail.

column3: W-DXF-SHED F3 (32 footings 48 x 60 in as drawn, centred on 32 columns, z -1.4478..-1.143) + H5/H6 (type name from the drawing's label)
column4: M: Convert. Columns and footings, as drawn.
column5: M: Convert. Thirty-two columns, thirty-two footings, as drawn. Each footing sits centred on its column, and the column keeps the drawing's own label as its type.

column3: recorder log §FILM_FACT ifc (IFC-SEED seeded=64 typed=64) + extractIFC2DB §SUMMARY elements=64
column4: M: The usual IFC export. Then our database format.
column5: M: Export the usual IFC, typed. Then the usual extractor to our database format: sixty-four elements. | F: Nothing special? | M: Nothing special.

column3: recorder log §FILM_FACT find (IfcColumn found=32, cost line) · viewer find_erp_push.js
column4: M: In the Viewer, Find a column. Its cost is there.
column5: M: In the Viewer, Find a column. Its cost is there, from the rates and the model's own quantities. | F: Whose rates? | M: The Viewer's. An estimate, not a tender.

column4: M: One click and it is an ERP order.
column5: M: One click on ERP pushes a project order, with a link into the iDempiere project window. | F: So it is ERP ready? | M: Ready for the ERP, yes.

column3: lane §L7 (not done: beams, grade beams, trusses, roof, doors; reasons in the lane doc)
column4: M: Columns and footings only. The rest needs the owner.
column5: M: This is columns and footings only. Beams, trusses and the roof need facts the drawing does not state. | F: So not finished? | M: Not finished. And the cost is an estimate, not a tender.
